national.title: How to Apply for a Death Certificate in India (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step guide to registering a death and obtaining an official death certificate on the Civil Registration System portal. Verified statutory fee rules under the RBD Act, medical certificate requirements, and delayed registration steps.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4 / 4A)
steps.description: Collect Form 4 (institutional death) or Form 4A (non-institutional death) signed by the registered attending medical doctor.
steps.calloutText: Ensure Form 4 contains the registered doctor's medical council registration number and official hospital stamp.

steps.title: Collect Crematorium or Burial Ground Receipt
steps.description: Obtain the official receipt stating deceased name, date, time, and cremation or burial registry entry.
steps.calloutText: Most municipal registrars mandate the cremation receipt as primary proof of disposal of mortal remains.

steps.title: Inform Local Registrar of Births and Deaths Within 21 Days
steps.description: Submit death intimation within 21 days to ensure zero late fee and immediate registry recording.
steps.where: Local Municipal Ward Office / Gram Panchayat
steps.calloutText: Registration within 21 days is free of cost and avoids cumbersome magistrate permission procedures.

steps.title: Fill Death Registration Report (Form 2)
steps.description: Enter deceased's full legal name, gender, age at death, date of death, place of death, and permanent residential address.
steps.where: Official CRS Portal (crsorgi.gov.in) or Municipal Office

steps.title: Enter Informant and Next of Kin Details
steps.description: Provide the informant's name, relationship to the deceased, 12-digit Aadhaar number, and active mobile number.

steps.title: Upload Supporting Documents and Receipts
steps.description: Upload scanned copies of Form 4, crematorium receipt, deceased Aadhaar, and informant identity proof in PDF format.

steps.title: Pay Statutory Delayed Fee (Only If After 21 Days)
steps.description: Registration within 21 days is free. If delayed beyond 21 days, pay the nominal statutory fee of ₹2 to ₹20.

steps.title: Receive Digitally Signed Death Certificate
steps.description: Download the digitally signed QR-coded death certificate from the portal or collect the physical embossed copy from the Registrar.
steps.where: CRS Citizen Portal / Municipal Civic Counter

rejectionReasons.title: Spelling Mismatch Between Doctor's Certificate and Aadhaar
rejectionReasons.description: Discrepancy in the spelling of the deceased person's name between Form 4 and Aadhaar halts registration.
rejectionReasons.solution: Ensure the attending hospital records the deceased's name exactly as printed on their Aadhaar card.

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Crematorium or Cemetery Receipt
rejectionReasons.description: Failing to attach the official receipt proving physical cremation or burial leads to immediate scrutiny rejection.
rejectionReasons.solution: Obtain the formal numbered receipt from the crematorium authority before filing Form 2.

rejectionReasons.title: Unnatural Death Reported Without Police Panchnama
rejectionReasons.description: Registering a death resulting from an accident, poisoning, or suicide without police clearance is prohibited.
rejectionReasons.solution: Obtain certified copies of the police FIR, panchnama, and post-mortem report before applying.

rejectionReasons.title: Delayed Registration Beyond 1 Year Without SDM Order
rejectionReasons.description: Submitting a death report after one year without an inquiry order from the Executive Magistrate violates Section 13(3).
rejectionReasons.solution: File an application before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate to obtain the mandatory court order.

rejectionReasons.title: Contradictory Date or Time of Death Across Documents
rejectionReasons.description: A discrepancy between the hospital death time and crematorium entry time blocks electronic approval.
rejectionReasons.solution: Ensure that the hospital summary, doctor's certificate, and crematorium slip record consistent timelines.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying Outside Proper Municipal Ward Jurisdiction
rejectionReasons.description: Submitting the death intimation to a municipality where the death did not physically occur causes jurisdiction rejection.
rejectionReasons.solution: Submit Form 2 strictly to the Registrar having jurisdiction over the physical place where death occurred.

faqItems.question: Is death registration free of cost in India?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Registration within 21 days is 100% free, and the first certificate copy is provided free under Section 12.

faqItems.question: Within how many days must a death be registered?
faqItems.answer: Under the RBD Act 1969, a death must be reported to the local Registrar within 21 days of occurrence.

faqItems.question: Who is legally responsible for reporting a death?
faqItems.answer: The head of the household for home deaths, or the medical officer in charge for hospital institutional deaths.

faqItems.question: What is a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD)?
faqItems.answer: Form 4 / 4A signed by a registered doctor certifying the medical cause of death for national vital statistics.

faqItems.question: How can I register a death after more than one year has passed?
faqItems.answer: You must obtain an inquiry order from an Executive Magistrate (SDM) under Section 13(3) of the Act.

faqItems.question: Can I download a death certificate online?
faqItems.answer: Yes. If the death is registered on the Civil Registration System, download the QR-coded digital certificate using OTP.

faqItems.question: Why is a cremation or burial receipt mandatory for death registration?
faqItems.answer: The receipt provides physical verification that the mortal remains were legally consigned to the ground or cremated.

faqItems.question: How many copies of the death certificate should I obtain?
faqItems.answer: It is advisable to obtain 5 to 10 certified copies for bank accounts, insurance claims, property transfer, and pensions.

GJ.title: How to Get a Death Certificate in Gujarat (2026)
GJ.summary: In Gujarat, deaths are recorded online via e-Nagar across urban municipalities and through Talati-cum-Mantri at Gram Panchayats. Digital bilingual certificates are issued in Gujarati and English with verifiable QR codes.
GJ.verifiedBy: Civic Research Editorial Team - Gujarat Bureau

steps.title: Obtain Hospital Cause of Death Slip or Smashan Receipt
steps.description: Collect Form 4 medical cause of death from the attending hospital or obtain an official crematorium receipt from the registered Moksha Dham.
steps.where: Hospital Medical Records or Municipal Crematorium
steps.calloutText: The municipal crematorium or burial ground receipt is mandatory evidence for non-institutional deaths across Gujarat.

steps.title: Access Gujarat e-Nagar or Visit Local Gram Panchayat
steps.description: Urban residents log into the e-Nagar portal or visit municipal civic centers. Rural residents contact the Gram Panchayat Talati-cum-Mantri.

steps.title: Submit Form 2 Death Registration Application
steps.description: Enter deceased details including full name in Gujarati and English, date of passing, exact place of death, and informant relationship.
steps.calloutText: Cross-check spellings against the deceased person's Aadhaar and property records to ensure smooth inheritance transfers.

steps.title: Upload Informant Identity Proof and Supporting Slips
steps.description: Upload scanned copies of informant Aadhaar card, deceased person identity proof, and the doctor certification or crematorium voucher.

steps.title: Talati Panchnama or Executive Magistrate Sanction
steps.description: Rural home deaths require a spot panchnama signed by two local panchas. Deaths over one year old require a Mamlatdar court order.
steps.where: Village Panchayat or Taluka Mamlatdar Office
steps.calloutText: Under Section 13(3) of the RBD Act, registrations after one year require formal permission from the Executive Magistrate.

steps.title: Download QR-Coded Bilingual Death Certificate
steps.description: Upon verification by the municipal health registrar, download your digitally signed certificate directly from e-Nagar or collect at civic desk.
steps.calloutText: Gujarat death certificates contain cryptographically signed QR codes for instant online verification by banks and insurance firms.

fees.label: Timely Registration Fee (Within 21 Days)
fees.description: Statutory registration and first certified copy is free within 21 days of passing.

fees.label: Additional Certified Copy Fee
fees.description: Prescribed statutory charge per additional certified copy under Gujarat RBD Rules.

fees.label: Late Registration Penalty (After 30 Days)
fees.description: Statutory delayed registration fine prescribed under Gujarat state vital statistics rules.

faqItems.question: Is the crematorium receipt mandatory for death certificate in Gujarat?
faqItems.answer: Yes. For deaths taking place at home, the official Moksha Dham or burial ground receipt is mandatory evidence.

faqItems.question: Can I download a death certificate online via Gujarat e-Nagar?
faqItems.answer: Yes. You can search digitized municipal death records by date and registration number to download signed e-certificates.

faqItems.question: What is the fee for additional copies of a death certificate in Gujarat?
faqItems.answer: Each additional certified copy costs five rupees under Gujarat Registration of Births and Deaths Rules.

faqItems.question: What is the process if a death occurred at home in rural Gujarat?
faqItems.answer: Inform the village Talati-cum-Mantri within 21 days with the crematorium receipt and two local witness statements.
